newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy needs more measures to cut spending - Fazio.
newsitem.headline: Italy needs more measures to cut spending - Fazio.

text.p: Italy needs to push through structural measures curtailing spending on health and pensions in order to achieve a lasting improvement in public finances, Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said in an interview.

"What is needed, generally speaking, is a structural and hence, lasting equilibrium of the public finances. Investors will not be satisfied with temporary measures," Fazio told British financial publication Euromoney.
A copy of the interview was released by the Bank of Italy on Tuesday in advance of the magazine's publication on Wednesday. Euromoney has chosen Fazio as its central banker of the year.
Fazio said despite a recent reform of Italy's pensions system, more savings were needed.

"In the pension system, imbalances can be quite significant in the long run. The system has just been comprehensively reformed, but it will be necessary to tighten some parameters in the near future," said Fazio in the interview in August.

The government will unveil its 1997 budget proposals this week. Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has called for cuts in spending on health and pensions, but prime minister Romano Prodi has said they will be left unscathed.

Fazio also singled out waste, misallocation of resources and tax evasion as targets for action. "Public health services are a prime candidate. Another field is tax collection. Tax evasion is equal to several percentage points of GDP," he said.
The welfare system granted excessive benefits to high income earners, said Fazio.

"There is a need for a revision which will eliminate widespread inefficiencies, together with certain excessive benefits for the high-income brackets. The benefits will have to be focused on the lower income brackets," said Fazio.
Fazio also appealed for wage restrain among public sector employees.
"The expansion of the wage bill of the public sector must continue to be marked by the same moderation as it has shown over the last few years," he added. Milan newsroom +392-66102321
